about.title: Whittier Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should not become your problem to prove. In Whittier, that might be a space heater that ignites in an apartment off Beverly Boulevard, a ladder that buckles during a weekend project, or a child's car seat that comes apart in a fender-bender on Painter Avenue. California treats most of these claims under strict liability. Instead of showing that a company was careless, you generally need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. The reach of that rule is wide: the manufacturer, the distributor, and the store on Whittier Boulevard that sold it may each share responsibility. Whittier's 87,438 residents buy the same tools, appliances, medications, and vehicles as the rest of Los Angeles County, and when one of them fails, our team handles these cases on contingency at no upfront cost. Keep the product. Do not repair, return, or discard it.

Airbag, seat belt, and tire failure injuries in crashes

items.title: Strict Liability Understood
items.desc: Our team knows that California generally requires proof of a defect and causation, not proof of negligence. That framing shapes how a claim is built from the first conversation.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers may all be held responsible under California law. We can examine each of them rather than settling for the nearest name on the receipt.

items.title: Evidence Comes First
items.desc: The product itself is often the case. We advise quickly on preserving it, and there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was negligent?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability commonly runs on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company meant well or acted carelessly is often beside the point. We can tell you which theory fits your situation.

items.question: A part on my car failed in a crash on Lambert Road. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both. Whittier recorded 443 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes involve a defective airbag, brake, or tire alongside a driver's mistake. A product liability claim can be brought against the manufacturer or seller even while a separate claim runs against another driver. Keep the vehicle and the failed part exactly as they are until we have weighed in.

items.question: I threw away the packaging. Can I still bring a claim in Whittier?
items.answer: Possibly. The product itself matters most, so hold onto it in its current condition and photograph everything you still have. Receipts, bank statements, and photos of where you bought it can help trace the retailer and distributor. We can review what remains at no cost and assess your case.
